args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, was also unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What went wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also failed in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. A status check afterwards shows all three regions on v2.3.0, reporting healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident INC-0001:** It describes the failure, the rollback and the current healthy state. It also says the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before v2.3.1 is deployed again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
